column1: # docs/OPENER-FAST-FORWARD-SWEEP.tsv — the 72-opener fast-forward sweep (ADR-0264).
# WHAT IT ANSWERS. "Play battle N" is a seek into the navigator, and a seek settles
# the battle world by replaying that group's OPENER at 30x
# (`NavigatorMain._settle_world_via_opener`). The replay is bounded by
# `ScenarioPathApplier._MAX_FF_FRAMES = 2100` host frames — a cap that had never been
# exercised across the range it now carries, and that fails SILENTLY: a truncated
# fast-forward leaves the world on whichever `{19}` it reached, which is an authored
# camera pose, just not the one the battle opens on.
# THE ANSWER: 72 of 72 openers reach their main context's `Event End`, and the cap is
# not close. Worst case is root 291 (Riovanes rooftop, scn 292, 564 instructions) at
# 169 frames — 8% of the budget, 1,931 frames of margin. Mean 46.9, min 13. The
# LONGEST opener is not the slowest one: root 166's scn 167 is 679 instructions and
# settles in 145 frames, because the cost is the stream's BLOCKING time (waits, camera
# lerp durations, unit motion), not its length.
# TAKEN 2026-09-08 on the 4.8 fork, one Godot process per group, the way a player
# launches one:
#     uv run python tools/sweep_opener_fast_forward.py --jobs 4 \
#         --out docs/OPENER-FAST-FORWARD-SWEEP.tsv
# The tool exits non-zero if any group fails to settle, so re-running it IS the check.
# ⚠️ THE FIRST TAKE READ 71/72, AND THE ONE FAILURE WAS THE INSTRUMENT. Root 46's
# opener (scn 47) ends `{E3} Event End 2` at pc 131 followed by a `{DB} Event End` at
# 132 that is therefore never dispatched — so a fast-play watching only the PC sat on
# 132 for its whole 150-frame stall budget after the scenario had already finished, and
# reported `stalled`. `ScenarioVM.is_main_context_finished()` now answers the question
# the normal-speed walk actually asks (did the main context run its Event End?), which
# both corrected the reading and gave that one seek 2.5 s back.
# COLUMNS. `frames` is host frames spent in the fast-forward; `outcome` is
# `ScenarioPathApplier.FfOutcome` — `ended` is the only settled result. `margin_frames`
# = cap - frames.
